pamphlet_excerpts: AKC Recognized Breed Groups: The groups, and many of the breeds within these groups, recognized by the AKC are as follows (p. 12).
Sporting Group Hunting Skills: These are dogs that "scent" and either track, point, or flush (reveal a bird's location and cause it to fly), and retrieve game birds on land or in water (p. 12).
Controlled Breeding and Selection: The wide range of shape, size, color, and personality of purebred dogs is the result of controlled breeding and selection (p. 12).
Specialized Working Canine Roles: Some dogs were bred to hunt, some to serve as guard or sled dogs, and some to be herders (p. 12).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Examine Selective Breeding Traits: The wide range of shape, size, color, and personality of purebred dogs is the result of controlled breeding and selection (p. 12).
Step 2 - Identify Traditional Canine Jobs: Some dogs were bred to hunt, some to serve as guard or sled dogs, and some to be herders (p. 12).
Step 3 - Classify Breeds by Function: In the late 1800s, at the same time that dog shows we regaining popularity, a system was developed for classifying breeds according to how they are used (p. 12).
Step 4 - Review AKC Registry Standards: In the United States, the American Kennel Club has maintained a registry of breeds since 1884 (p. 12).

quiz_item.question: When observing an unfamiliar dog in Dog Care Requirement 1, which combination of canine body language signals indicates the dog is fearful, stressed, or defensive and should not be crowded?
options: A. Ears pinned flat back, tail tucked tightly between the legs, stiff posture, raised hackles, whale eye (showing the whites of the eyes), lip licking, or a low growl.
B. A loose, wiggly body posture with a play bow (front elbows on the ground, hindquarters raised) and a relaxed, open mouth.
C. Sitting calmly at the handler's side with soft eyes, neutral ear position, and gentle tail wagging at mid-level.
D. Rolling onto its side in a quiet home living room to fall asleep after eating dinner.
choices: A. Ears pinned flat back, tail tucked tightly between the legs, stiff posture, raised hackles, whale eye (showing the whites of the eyes), lip licking, or a low growl.

quiz_item.correct_answer: A. Ears pinned flat back, tail tucked tightly between the legs, stiff posture, raised hackles, whale eye (showing the whites of the eyes), lip licking, or a low growl.

pamphlet_excerpts: Nationwide Heartworm Disease Risk: Keeping Your Dog Healthy. heartworm society. org Heart worm disease can affect dogs in every state (p. 57).
Intestinal Parasite Transmission Routes: In adult dogs most intestinal parasites are picked up from the stool of an infected dog (except tapeworms, which are spread by fleas) (p. 57).
Biannual Fecal Screening Checks: Because this can easily happen when dogs are sniffing around outside, adult dogs should also have a stool check a couple of times a year to screen (p. 57).
Microscopic Internal Parasite Detection: Remember, most internal parasites are not visible to the nakedeye, so don't assume they are not a problem just because you don't see them (p. 57).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Schedule Fecal Screening Checks: Because this can easily happen when dogs are sniffing around outside, adult dogs should also have a stool check a couple of times a year to screen (p. 57).
Step 2 - Screen for Hidden Parasites: Remember, most internal parasites are not visible to the nakedeye, so don't assume they are not a problem just because you don't see them (p. 57).
Step 3 - Prevent Mosquito Heartworm Bites: Dogs can get heart worms through the bite of a mosquito that carries the parasite (p. 57).
Step 4 - Test Early for Heartworms: A dog might be infected for a longtime before you know about it because it takes awhile for the worms to cause damage to the dog's heart (p. 57).

pamphlet_excerpts: Mia cis Early Carnivore Ancestor: The origin of dogs can be traced to an animal called Mia cis, which looked more like a weasel than a dog (p. 9).
Prehistoric Carnivore Physical Traits: This small, flesh-eating creature had short legs, a long tail, five toes, and teeth like those of today's carnivores (p. 9).
Cynodictis Canine Dentition Traits: The next important ancestor, called Cynodictis was the first to have doglikecharacteristics, such as a shortened fifth toe, 42 teeth, and longer legs (p. 9).
Tomarctus Modern Dog Resemblance: Then came a descendent of Cynodictis, called Tomarctus, which resembled today's dogs (p. 9).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Trace Early Canine Dentition: The next important ancestor, called Cynodictis was the first to have doglikecharacteristics, such as a shortened fifth toe, 42 teeth, and longer legs (p. 9).
Step 2 - Compare Tomarctus Physical Features: Then came a descendent of Cynodictis, called Tomarctus, which resembled today's dogs (p. 9).
Step 3 - Identify Evolved Dewclaw Anatomy: This animal had short, erect ears, long legs and tail, and adewclaw that had developed from the shortened fifth toe (p. 9).
Step 4 - Observe Modern Canine Instincts: Also, Tomarctus probably behaved much like today's dogs (p. 9).

choices: A. Ears pinned flat back, tail tucked tightly between the legs, stiff posture, raised hackles, whale eye (showing the whites of the eyes), lip licking, or a low growl.
